turns.t: Hello, doctor, I got this letter about my eyes, the screening, the photos, and I've brought it but I can't find my glasses, so I can't read it.
No problem, I've got the result on screen. The screening shows early changes at the back of your eyes from the diabetes.
Oh no. Does that mean I'm going blind? ~
No, not at all. It's the earliest stage, called background retinopathy. Tiny changes in the small blood vessels, and your vision isn't affected yet.
Right. Well, I do get blurry some days.
Tell me about the blurriness.
Mostly the afternoon, when I've been at the computer. Things go fuzzy for a bit, then clear up.
Any floaters, or flashing lights?
No flashing. A few floaters, I think, but they've been there for years.
Any pain in your eyes, or loss of part of your vision?
No, no pain. No loss, nothing like that.
Now the diabetes treatment. What are you taking for it?
Metformin. 1000 mg, twice a day, I think. I'm honestly not sure of the dose, my wife organises it. And if I'm honest, I miss the evening one a lot.
So the plan is twice a day, 1000 mg as you recall it, but some evenings it's missed. That's honest, thank you.
I don't want to get a row. ~
No row. It's the control that matters, so we'll try to make it easier. Any allergies I should know about?
Sulfa drugs, but only as a child. I came out in a rash, and I've never had one since. They told my mum to keep me away from them.
Thank you. Let me check your pulse and pressure. ~
Please, go on. ~
Pulse 78, blood pressure 136 over 84.
Good? ~
Good enough. For the eyes, the best treatment is good control of your sugar and blood pressure. ~
I'll try, I promise. ~
I'd like to arrange an HbA1c blood test, to see how your sugar has averaged over the last three months.
Right. And what about my eyes? ~
You'll be invited for screening again in twelve months, and we'll catch any change early. ~
Twelve months. Good, that's not too soon. ~
And for the evening metformin, try taking it with your evening meal, rather than later, or set a phone alarm.
I can set an alarm. My wife will love that. ~
Make sure you get your eyes checked at the optician too, and find those glasses. ~
They're probably in the fridge. ~
It's happened before. Mind how you go. ~

chief_complaint.value: I got this letter about my eyes, the screening

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient gave the metformin dose tentatively ("I think... not sure of the dose").
Metformin is prescribed twice a day but the patient says he often misses the evening dose; actual adherence unknown.

clinical_actions.description: Take evening metformin with the evening meal or set a phone alarm
